samples.summary: The pixel hit-test affinity changes (the bulk of the diff) have no test that exercises them
samples.evidence: The diff adds `affinityForOffset`/`hitTestLineAffinity` wiring at four hit-test sites: the header/footer line hit-test (~text-editor.ts:4431), the merged-cell resolver (~4546), `resolveOffsetInCellAtPoint` (~4804) and `resolveOffsetInTableAtPoint` (~5003), plus new `lineAffinity` on `CellHitTest` fallbacks. The only new test file, packages/docs/test/view/cell-hf-wrap-affinity.test.ts, exercises (a) the pure helper `hitTestLineAffinity` with three literal-argument calls (lines 74-86) and (b) typing + End, which goes through `getWrapAffinity` (lines 144-187). Nothing dispatches a mouse event: grep for `mousedown|MouseEvent` across packages/docs/test matches only editor-contextmenu.test.ts, and no test references `resolveOffsetInCell`. So if any call site passed the wrong `lineStartOffset` or the wrong `isFirstLineOfBlock` (e.g. `li === 0` vs `li === blockStartLine`), every test in the suite would still pass — the unit tests of the helper cannot detect miswiring.

The mouse-move/drag branch now propagates the cell-local affinity onto the endpoint (`pos.lineAffinity` set at ~1866) and prefers it over `result.lineAffinity` at the `cursor.moveTo` call. No test simulates a drag: packages/docs/test contains no mousemove/mousedown-driven selection test (grep `MouseEvent` matched only editor-contextmenu.test.ts), and the new test file only uses `_setSelectionForTest` and keyboard events. A regression in this precedence (e.g. reverting to `result.lineAffinity`) would not be caught.

samples.summary: Intermediate assertion `offset === boundary` after typing is near-tautological setup, not behavior
samples.evidence: `place(editor, blockId, boundary - 1); await type(container, 'x'); expect(...offset).toBe(boundary);` holds for any working insertion (caret advances by one from boundary-1) regardless of affinity, so it asserts nothing about the change under review. It is harmless as a setup sanity check, but only the following `expect(...).toBeGreaterThan(boundary)` line actually discriminates the fixed behaviour from the old 'backward'-only behaviour.

samples.summary: No footer coverage despite the change and test doc claiming header/footer
samples.evidence: The test docblock (lines 9-19) and the describe title say 'table cell or a header/footer', but only 'header' is mounted (`_setEditContextForTest('header')`, line 184). The footer path (a separate active-layout region resolved by `getVisualLineRange`/`getActiveLayout`) is never exercised; a footer-specific lookup failure would go unnoticed.
